## What it is
Congestion control is a method used in computer networks to manage the flow of data packets, preventing performance degradation due to too many packets being processed at once. [p. 2]

## Real-life analogy
Imagine a water pipe where the flow of water is controlled by a valve. If too many people try to use the water at once, the pipe can become clogged, causing water to flow slowly. Congestion control works similarly, ensuring that no single part of the network becomes overwhelmed with too many packets. [p. 2]

## How it works
1. **Each host has a finite queue**: In a network, each device (host) has a limited amount of space to store incoming packets. When this space is full, any additional packets are discarded. [p. 2]
2. **Leaky bucket algorithm**: Think of a bucket with a small hole at the bottom. Water can pour in at any rate, but it leaks out at a constant rate. If the bucket is full, extra water spills out. In the network, each host has a finite queue: packets enter at any rate and are sent at a constant rate. When the queue is full, any additional packets are discarded. [p. 2]
3. **Token bucket algorithm**: Imagine a bucket with tokens generated at a fixed rate, one every T seconds. A packet can be sent only by taking a token. Idle hosts save tokens (up to the bucket size), so short bursts can be sent quickly. The token bucket allows bursts (the leaky bucket does not), and when the bucket is full, it discards tokens, not packets. [p. 2]

## Key terms
- **Leaky bucket**: A mechanism where packets are sent at a constant rate, and any excess packets are discarded. [p. 2]
- **Token bucket**: A mechanism where packets are sent only by taking a token, and idle hosts save tokens, allowing bursts to be sent quickly. [p. 2]

## Example
Consider a network with a leaky bucket algorithm. Suppose a host has a queue of 10 packets and the leaky bucket allows 5 packets per second. If 15 packets arrive in a second, 5 packets will be discarded because the queue is full. [p. 2]

## What to draw in the exam
No diagram needed. [p. 2]

## Exam tip
Examiners often ask about the differences between leaky bucket and token bucket algorithms, focusing on how they handle bursts and idle times. Understanding the mechanism and its effects on network performance is crucial. [p. 2]
